notes:
Commercial / technical notes:
- Account: Pelorus builds personalization and inline reranking for large retail site (peak sale events). heavy read/write to embedding store + rerank pipeline.
- Current infra: Mix of in-house TF for embeddings, but looking to migrate generation/rerank to Redwood Dedicated for predictable latency and ops overhead reduction.
- Main ask: throughput guarantee negotiations. procurement focused on min tokens/sec, concurrency caps, and burst policy for holiday peaks.
- From POC: sustained ~62k tokens/sec with current config; customer wants contractual min 75k aggregate tokens/sec with 10m burst to 180k. They insisted on p95 latency SLOs in contract.
- Pelorus engineering: "We need predictable throughput during flash sales or revenue loss is visible within minutes." — Head of ML (quote).
- Proposed Redwood responses: offer 75k sustained guarantee with defined concurrency cap 120, burst up to 250% (i.e., 187.5k) for 10min windows, automated warm-up policy and prefix/KV cache priming; penalties/credits tied to sustained shortfall >3 consecutive 10m windows.
- Important negotiation points: how bursts count against reserved capacity vs. pay-as-you-go; how autoscale headroom behaves when VPC private deployment has strict network egress limits; explicit cold-start delineation (what counts as outage vs. warm-up).
- Security: Pelorus requires SSO/SAML, KMS integration, SOC2 attestation, and optional EU data residency for subset of user data. Legal demands explicit audit log retention of 12 months.
- Ops ask: per-route token breakdown in Console; tracing hooks to pinpoint tail-latency causes during bursts.
- Commercial: target ARR band $400k-$800k, willing to sign 12–24 month reserved capacity if SLOs and burst terms acceptable.
- Next: update SLA draft with numeric throughput clauses, run one more POC with warmed caches (Dec 3), align legal on residency language (Dec 6), finance/pricing review (Dec 9).
- Quick win: offer a 30-day guaranteed warm-up window before high-traffic events (prep run) as part of onboarding to reduce cold-start spikes.
- Jira references for POC bugs: INFRA-9876 (GPU scheduling), INFRA-9890 (KV cache priming).
